subject: Dedicated capacity surge playbook — cross-functional alignment
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ops@cloudproc.example.com
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity surge playbook — initial ask
Attachments: capacity_request.xlsx, surge-playbook-draft.md

Team —

We have a time-sensitive POC with Helix Therapeutics (contact: Sarah Li) that will start next Tuesday, 4/19. They expect a concentrated 10-day spike of batch inference and distributed evals that will temporarily double their token throughput compared to the pilot baseline. Finance and sales have greenlit a short-term reservation but we need an ops + product playbook to make this safe and predictable.

High-level asks:
- Reserve a temporary dedicated slice (estimate: 6 A100-equivalent slots) for 10 days with an autoscale policy exception to prioritize Helix traffic.
- Draft runbook for surge: admission control thresholds, cache warming, fallback model variants, and post-surge reconciliation.
- Identify cost approval and who will own the reservation lifecycle (start/end).

I've attached the request workbook from Sales (capacity_request.xlsx) and a barebones playbook draft (surge-playbook-draft.md). Can ops/infra + product review and call out any blockers by EOD Monday (4/12)? Marissa — can you confirm the commercial window and opening for the reservation? Dev/Ben — is this feasible without a private deployment change?

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@helixthera.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity surge playbook — initial ask

Thanks Tessa —

Confirming commercial: Helix approved a 10-day reserved window billed as a short-term commit; legal/finance signed off on the SOW addendum. I'll attach the billing confirmation to the Deal record. We need to ensure we can guarantee SLA-like behavior for the window (predictable latency and no noisy-neighbor effects).

Two quick asks from Sales:
1) Product needs to tell us what behavior we should promise (p95 latency target, max concurrent requests, model variant fallback) so we can commit to Helix.
2) Ops wants a rollback condition in case the reservation harms other committed customers — please include a safety cutoff.

Dev — Ben — can you respond with an ops-ready plan? If this is simple (policy change + tagging + reserve), we can execute on Mon and stand up by Tue. If it requires infra changes, call it out now.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity surge playbook — initial ask

On Mon, Apr 11, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dev — Ben — can you respond with an ops-ready plan?

We ran a quick capacity check. Short answer: feasible without code changes if we approach as a temporary reservation + autoscale policy override on the existing dedicated pool. Practical notes:
- Need an explicit "surge-tag" on the pool to route Helix traffic and prioritize it in the scheduler.
- Autoscale exception: raise max-concurrent-batches and temporarily lower the batching timeout for that tag to reduce p95 latency for small requests. This is a config toggle (no kernel/runtime patch).
- KV cache warming: we should pre-warm prefixes for their main prompt sets to avoid cold-start tail latency on day 1. Ops will need a short preload job (script attached in playbook draft).

Questions for Sales/Product:
- Expected concurrency during peak (per second)? The capacity numbers change a lot if they're 50 req/s vs 5 req/s. The workbook currently has approximate QPS but can you confirm final numbers?
- Which model family should be favored for fallback? (We can route to a 4-bit quantized variant if cost matters.)

If we get QPS and model preference today, Ops can stage the reserve and pre-warm on Mon night.

— Dev
Lead Product Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@helixthera.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cloudproc.example.com
Date: 2027-04-12T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity surge playbook — initial ask

Thanks team —

Confirming Helix expectation: burst to ~18k tokens/sec peak across 6 concurrent workers for ~10 days (4/19–4/28). Model: helix-prod-v1 (we are OK with a quantized fallback for cost but want output parity validation before fallback). We can provide a frozen prompt set of 150 evals to use for cache warming.

Happy to hop on a short sync if useful.

— Sarah Li
Head of ML Ops, Helix Therapeutics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ops@cloudproc.example.com
Date: 2027-04-12T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity surge playbook — ops runbook (draft)
Attachments: surge-playbook-draft.md

Folks —

I've expanded the draft playbook with step-by-step ops actions and rollback criteria. Highlights:
- Prep (Mon night): tag pool "helix-surge-4_19", inject temporary autoscale policy, kick off KV pre-warm using the 150 frozen prompts.
- Day-of checks (Tue morning): run synthetic latency sweep (p50/p95), confirm worker affinity to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Runtime controls: if p95 > 2.0s for 15m and global impact detected (CPU/GPU steal > 10%), we throttle Helix traffic by fallback to a quantized variant and scale down reserved slots by 2.
- Post-surge: reconcile billing and remove tags; run a postmortem within 5 business days.

Open items for Product/Eng: exact p95 SLA to advertise (Dev suggested configuration to hit ~1.2s p95 given current kernel), and verification steps for output parity on quantized fallback.

Ben Carter
SRE, Dedicated Platform

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@helixthera.com>, ops@cloudproc.example.com
Date: 2027-04-13T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity surge playbook — cross-functional alignment

Thanks — this is great progress. Summary and next steps: 
1) Commercial confirmed by Marissa; Helix windows 4/19–4/28, 6-slot slice.
2) Dev confirms config-only approach; Dev/Ben will prepare the pool tag + autoscale override.
3) Sarah will drop the 150 frozen prompts into the shared Drive link (thanks).
4) Ben will run the pre-warm and the day-of synthetic sweep; rollback criteria documented in the playbook.
5) Karthik — please approve the short-term reservation and sign off on the cost / SLA tradeoff by EOD 4/14.

I'll open the Ops ticket (INF-934) and attach the finalized playbook and the signed SOW addendum. If anyone needs a quick sync, I'm free tomorrow morning.

Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
